headline: Margin jumps on timing of expenses; outlook broadly intact
summary_short: Netflix's Q3 2026 revenue was $12.87B (+11.8% y/y) with a 34.6% operating margin and diluted EPS of $0.87 versus $0.59; Q4 revenue is forecast at $13.4B.
summary_long: Operating income rose 37% to $4.46B, ahead of forecast mainly because of the timing of expenses. Revenue growth was driven by memberships, pricing and advertising, and churn improved. For Q4 Netflix forecasts operating margin of 26.0%, including about 120 bps from recent headcount reductions. For 2026 it expects revenue of $51.1B and a 31.5% operating margin, with ad revenue now about $2.7B versus roughly $3B before.
confidence_notes: Net income y/y and free cash flow y/y computed from the shareholder letter's quarterly table (3,664 vs 2,547; 2,884 vs 2,660). Netflix says its guidance is its actual internal forecast.

drivers.explanation: Revenue growth came mainly from subscription revenue on more members and higher prices, plus growth in advertising and favorable currency effects.
Margin was ahead of forecast primarily due to the timing of expenses and slight revenue upside.
Healthy retention in every region; global and US churn improved year over year and was better than forecast.
